# N8: Telemetry: one trace from action to save to result, nothing anyone types, nothing at all when switched off, and quiet when it can’t send

A check of the core ([the journeys](../journeys.md)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/notes/8-telemetry.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured, and a limit its words don’t give is added after it, in the script’s test (“its test: …”).

## What it checks

observability, release 1. Runs the demo from the build that has a database address (DOWN), so telemetry has somewhere to send, and catches every insert to the telemetry tables with Playwright routing. At a phone and a desktop width: [TELEMETRY-SIGNALS] [TELEMETRY-FLOWS] a check-in sends, in one trace, the action, its save timed as a CLIENT span, the page showing the result and the check-in flow's finish; every span is OpenTelemetry's shape. [TELEMETRY-PRIVACY] a distinctive string typed into the check-in and a comment (and put in a search) never appears in any request. [TELEMETRY-SWITCH] once an admin turns recording off on Workspace, nothing is sent, after a reload too, and Settings says it's off. [TELEMETRY-SIGNALS] when the telemetry tables answer 404 the app carries on with no error of its own in the console (the browser's own "Failed to load resource" network line is not the app's) and sends at most a request or two. [STALE-RELOAD] (review F16) when a part of the build has gone since the tab loaded (the Map's file answers 404, as after a deploy), the page reloads itself once at the same address and the Map draws; when it is still gone after that reload, the page shows "Something went wrong" instead of reloading again. Offline (#167's review), opening Help, a part that loads when opened, reloads nothing: the page says it needs a connection, and Try again opens Help once the connection is back.

## Where it looks

- 390 × 844, as chen, on a touch screen
- 1280 × 800, as chen
- 390 × 844, as grace, on a touch screen
- 1280 × 800, as grace

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day. {…} is a value the script works out as it runs.
